findings.title: The narrowed wipe can no longer clear a leftover projectTabs file whose suffix is not one of the five tabs, so any such file would be pushed to the store and re-pushed for good

evidence.value: makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True), then for each name in the folder delete it only when the name ends .json AND the suffix before .json is in TABS AND it is not about to be rewritten - where the base was shutil.rmtree(folder) followed by makedirs(folder)
app.spec.json and p.backlog.json are deletable; app.findings.json (intended), app.usage.json, app.json and stray.txt are not

evidence.field: live listing (read-only) of out/projectTabs and out/.pushed.json
evidence.value: 10 files, all five TABS suffixes for the two projects; no non-TABS leftover exists today, so nothing is actually stranded

findings.impact: Narrowing the wipe is the right fix for CR-011-4 and the docstring was corrected to match, but the folder is no longer self-cleaning: a file left by a retired or renamed tab suffix now survives every run, refresh.py would push it as a projectTabs document and, once pushed, keep it alive. Nothing produces such a file today, and the pre-existing test that a dropped project loses its tabs still passes, so this is a hygiene gap, not wrong behaviour on merge.
findings.remediation: Either delete every .json in the folder that is neither an owned TAB about to be rewritten nor a suffix another exporter is registered as owning (a small OWNED_ELSEWHERE tuple next to TABS makes the ownership explicit in one place), or record in the docstring that a retired tab suffix must be removed by hand once. A test that plants a stale usage-suffixed file and asserts the intended outcome would pin whichever rule is chosen.

findings.title: A work item can be published as reaching GO while its ledger still lists findings open, because a GO round that carried no findings block is not authoritative for resolution, and the page shows both without explaining the mismatch

evidence.value: latest_ids comes from the last round that carried a findings block, while go_at is the first round whose kind is go, whatever it carried - the two read different rounds

evidence.field: export_sessions.main run against the real transcripts into a scratch out/ (read-only probe)
evidence.value: dispatch-board PBI-013: rounds 2, roundsToGo 1, open CR-PBI013-06; PBI-024: rounds 2, roundsToGo 1, three open. The page then renders N review rounds - reached GO at round 1 beside an Open tag.
the panel subtitle appends reached GO at round N whenever roundsToGo is set, with no interaction with the open list

findings.impact: Conservative and deliberate - refusing to resolve findings on a round it could not read is exactly the CR-011-2 fix, and leaving them open is the safe direction - but the published document can carry a combination a reader will take as a contradiction. F-3 asks only that a work item that has reached GO shows its rounds-to-GO, which it does, so this is presentation, not a broken criterion.
findings.remediation: Either word the subtitle so the two facts do not collide (naming the round the findings below came from), or state the rule in the findings_doc docstring and in the tab help text. No code-path change is needed.
refs: Correctness: contract reasoning against PBI-011 F-3

findings.title: A finding whose id is JSON null slips past the new id-less-finding drop and is published with the literal id None

evidence.value: the id is coerced with str() using an empty-string default and then tested for emptiness; the default only fires when the key is absent, so a present-but-null id becomes the truthy string None and is kept
findings_of on a fenced block whose findings list holds one object with a null id returns one entry whose id is the string None and whose other fields are empty

findings.impact: The collapse CR-011-8 set out to prevent still happens for this one shape: several null-id findings in one round all become the single entry None. Our own reviewers emit the required id, so this needs a malformed report to reach, and the outcome is a cosmetic row rather than a wrong open or resolved verdict.
findings.remediation: Coerce from a checked value rather than from the default (treat a null id as absent), or skip a finding whose id is not a non-empty string. One line, and the existing id-less-finding test gains a null-id case.
refs: Correctness: robustness at an input boundary (CWE-20 class, internal and trusted source)
